content.rendered:
Jeremiah prophesied to a nation with corrupt kings and false shepherds, and named the coming Branch by a single, decisive title: The Lord Our Righteousness.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, August 17, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“In His days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell safely; Now this is His name by which He will be called: THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.”
Jeremiah 23:6 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Jeremiah 23 opens with a woe against the shepherds of Israel who had scattered and destroyed the flock instead of tending it — corrupt kings, false prophets, leadership that had failed the people God entrusted to them. Into that failure, God promises a different kind of King: a righteous Branch from David’s line, who would reign wisely and execute justice, in whose days Judah would be saved and Israel would dwell in safety. And His name would be Jehovah Tsidkenu — the Lord our righteousness.

Notice what the name does not say. It does not say “the Lord who demands our righteousness” or “the Lord who grades our righteousness.” It says the Lord is our righteousness — not a standard we are measured against from a distance, but a righteousness given, supplied, credited to those who could never produce enough of their own. This is the same truth Paul would later unpack in full: “For He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him” (2 Corinthians 5:21).

The New King James rendering keeps the name in capitals for emphasis, exactly as the original text does: “THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS” (Jeremiah 23:6 NKJV). It is not a footnote name. It is the headline. Every failed shepherd in Jeremiah’s day, every corrupt king, every broken human system of justice, was answered by God supplying what none of them could: a righteousness that did not originate in human performance.

This matters for anyone who has ever tried and failed to be good enough — for God, for a parent, for their own conscience. Jehovah Tsidkenu is not a name that asks you to try harder. It is a name that tells you the righteousness you need has already been supplied by Another, and it is now yours by faith, not by performance. The Branch Jeremiah foresaw came, lived the righteous life none of us could live, and gave that righteousness to everyone who trusts Him.

Whatever failure or shame is whispering that you are not enough today, answer it with this name. Your righteousness was never meant to come from you. It comes from Him.

Prayer

Father, You are Jehovah Tsidkenu, my righteousness. I lay down every attempt to earn what You have already given. I receive by faith the righteousness of Christ, not my own performance, as the ground I stand on. Silence every voice that tells me I am not enough. In Him, I am righteous. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My God is Jehovah Tsidkenu. He is my righteousness, not my own effort. I am the righteousness of God in Christ. I stand before Him not on my performance but on His finished work.
